subject.title: build(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept these exact upstream action revisions in workflows that handle GitHub App private keys, repository tokens, and Codex automation?
rationale: This is an intentional third-party-code trust decision for credential-bearing workflow execution; patch review cannot safely substitute for the repository owner’s accepted-action policy.

options.title: Approve exact revisions after verification
options.body: A workflow-security owner verifies the cited upstream release commits and accepts the updated pins, with a redacted trusted final-head workflow result attached.

options.title: Split sensitive action updates
options.body: Land only the reviewed low-privilege action revisions and defer GitHub App token, Docker publishing, and Codex action updates to separately approved PRs.

options.title: Pause this grouped update
options.body: Close or defer the Dependabot batch and regenerate narrower updates after the trusted-action review path is available.

recommendation.title: Approve exact revisions after verification
recommendation.body: A workflow-security owner verifies the cited upstream release commits and accepts the updated pins, with a redacted trusted final-head workflow result attached.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the only concretely attributed actor available in the supplied item history; a human workflow-security owner must be identified before acting on the decision.
